The 3 AM Page That Changed Everything
Our e-commerce checkout service was dying. 500 requests per second. Thread pool exhausted. Response times spiking to 8 seconds during sales events. Customers abandoning carts.
The “fix” our team knew: rewrite everything reactive. WebFlux. Mono. Flux. Callback hell. Six months of refactoring for a team that breathes Spring MVC.
Then Java 21 shipped with virtual threads. One configuration change. One property. One restart.
500 RPS became 5,000 RPS. Response times dropped from 8 seconds to 200ms. We killed 30% of our cloud instances.
This is the story of how virtual threads work — and why they make reactive programming obsolete for most Java backends.
The Problem: Platform Threads Are Too Heavy
Traditional Java threads are OS threads. Each one costs ~1–2MB of stack space. On a 16GB server, that’s maybe 8,000 threads before you hit memory limits.
